headline: A first run that explains itself
items: A Getting Started wizard runs on a first launch. It has one job - installing the DSPi firmware on your Pico and confirming it came back running - and it hands you the console the moment that is done. Skippable in one click, and rerunnable from the Help menu.

Firmware Update now installs. Put a board into bootloader mode, or let the app restart the connected device into it, and Console writes the matching firmware and confirms the device came back running it.
Console ships the firmware it expects. The RP2040 and RP2350 images are bundled, so the app and the device can no longer drift apart.
A banner appears if a connected device is running a different firmware version, with a one-click update. It stays out of the way when the versions agree.
Version numbers are now plain point releases. Beta suffixes are gone, because a device can only report three numbers and two builds sharing a version cannot be told apart.
A short tour of the main window is offered once, covering channels, the graph, filters, volume, and the difference between changing something and committing it. Esc leaves it at any point.
Specialist features now introduce themselves the first time you open them, one card each, rather than being explained up front when they would mean nothing.
A Help menu, with Getting Started, the tour, release notes and documentation.
